pr_title: Avoid warnings for non-system indexes using `fast_refresh`
pr_body:
`LogsdbIndexModeSettingsProvider` creates a transient `MappingService` to check the index mappings for information relevant to `logsdb` mode. This may trigger unrelated warnings, e.g. for non-system indexes configured with `[fast_refresh=true]`. To avoid the noise, we can always unset this setting as it's not relevant to the `logsdb` functionality.

Fixes #124284

issue_context.title: LogsdbIndexModeSettingsProvider generates unnecesary warnings for system indices
issue_context.body:
When generating `MappingHints`, `LogsdbIndexModeSettingsProvider` [calls](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/b02f15d0094a7223f2a5f513acfc08d082e9325a/x-pack/plugin/logsdb/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/logsdb/LogsdbIndexModeSettingsProvider.java#L251) `IndicesService#createIndexMapperServiceForValidation` with a dummy indexMetadata that takes the real index name but does not replicate all the actual index settings. This can creae conflicting IndexMetadata for system indices with `fast_refresh=true` but `isSystem=false` which leads to exception being thrown in [IndexSettings](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/b02f15d0094a7223f2a5f513acfc08d082e9325a/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/index/IndexSettings.java#L1059-L1060).

An sample stacktrace is as the follows:
```
[2025-03-06T14:31:20,750][WARN ][o.e.x.l.LogsdbIndexModeSettingsProvider] [es01] unable to create mapper service for index [.security-profile-8] java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: index.fast_refresh is allowed only for system indices
	at org.elasticsearch.server@9.1.0/org.elasticsearch.index.IndexSettings.<init>(IndexSettings.java:1064)
	at org.elasticsearch.server@9.1.0/org.elasticsearch.indices.IndicesService.createIndexMapperServiceForValidation(IndicesService.java:855)
	at org.elasticsearch.xpack.logsdb.LogsdbIndexModeSettingsProvider.getMappingHints(LogsdbIndexModeSettingsProvider.java:250)
	at org.elasticsearch.xpack.logsdb.LogsdbIndexModeSettingsProvider.getAdditionalIndexSettings(LogsdbIndexModeSettingsProvider.java:115)
	at org.elasticsearch.server@9.1.0/org.elasticsearch.cluster.metadata.MetadataCreateIndexService.aggregateIndexSettings(MetadataCreateIndexService.java:1086)
	at org.elasticsearch.server@9.1.0/org.elasticsearch.cluster.metadata.MetadataCreateIndexService.applyCreateIndexRequestForSystemIndex(MetadataCreateIndexService.java:785)
	at org.elasticsearch.server@9.1.0/org.elasticsearch.cluster.metadata.MetadataCreateIndexService.applyCreateIndexRequest(MetadataCreateIndexService.java:434)
...
```

Relates: #118968
comments: @ywangd is `fast_refresh` the only setting you noticed causing such warnings? We can always set it to false in this context, since we only care for the mappings.
It is the only thing that I am aware so far. Let me ping @azasypkin who spotted this initially.

review_comments: Is there a relative easy way to test the problem reported in the issue?
It's a warning.. I tried to reproduce but it probably needs more than just the setting. @ywangd too for ideas.

The warning is for serverless deployments since `fast_refresh` was a [feature for serverless only](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/b02f15d0094a7223f2a5f513acfc08d082e9325a/x-pack/plugin/security/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/security/support/SecuritySystemIndices.java#L919-L925). In a serverless deployment, you can trigger this warning by just creating a related system index, e.g.

```
PUT .security-profile-8
```

In theory, the alternative fix can be removing the `fast_refresh` setting from all system indices since the setting is a noop today. But I am not sure whether that could still have other implications. Overall fixing it here feels safer.
I stand corrected, it's not just a warning - the provider doesn't work correctly when this trips. Not a real issue as system indexes are not in logsdb mode, but still easy to test.
